title: AI captions added unsupported detail in the middle and more reference-unmatched content near the end
summary: In long captions for 198 images, six AI models produced more reference-unsupported specifics in the middle. The mean share assigned to a residual reference-unmatched category rose from 10.3% in the first quarter to 28.1% in the last. This category need not mean that a sentence is objectively vague.
ai_technology: Qwen3-based claim extraction and verification; Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and LLaVA captioners
organization: Beihang University; Kuaishou Technology; Fudan University; Zhejiang University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §3, Figure 1/Table 1, appendix comparison to 347 human rubric judgments and sampled visual recheck

evidence.tested: Researchers divided captions into quarters, assessed claims against human-derived image rubrics, and checked a sample of verifier judgments with human reviewers.
evidence.unknown: A caption can include a true detail omitted from its reference. The reported pattern concerns this sample and reference-based labeling, with only sampled image-level checks.
evidence.ai_role: Qwen models extract and verify ordered atomic claims from human references and generated captions; human annotators validate a sample of judgments.
